description:
About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care into the one-stop shop for all home services. Getting there depends on how fast we can test, learn, and scale what works.

About The Data Team

We're a high-leverage team of Product Data Analysts embedded across the business, owning the semantic layer and the metrics everyone trusts. The experimentation program runs on real rigor, not vibes: pre-registered analysis plans gate every test launch, anytime-valid statistics keep mid-run dashboards honest under continuous viewing, automated daily SRM and attribution health sweeps catch broken tests early, and seasonal power forecasting accounts for a business that swings hard by time of year. The test lifecycle, design through readout, is already AI-driven. Our analysts are stretched across product, so Growth support has stayed part-time and reactive, until now.

The Role

You're the first data analyst dedicated entirely to Growth and Experimentation. Your primary charter is the experimentation program: test design, statistical rigor, and readouts across web funnels, SMS/drip, sales-driven tests, and SEO tests built on our own page-clustering tooling. It's a wider surface than most companies run. You also own the acquisition-to-conversion funnel those tests move, across paid, organic, and partner channels. What to test and which direction to bet on is the CRO's and Growth PMs' call; you shape it, they decide it.

You're not starting from scratch. Dashboards, tooling, and rigor scaffolding are already shipped and running. Expect the early months to be hands-on and manual: scoping tests, crunching readouts, while you build toward a self-serve layer. If a test readout and a funnel refresh ever compete for your week, the test wins.

What Makes This Role Different


The CEO personally engages with test design here: real organizational weight, no fight for buy-in
You partner directly with the Director of CRO, performance marketing, and Growth PMs, who come to you when a test needs a call


Requirements

What You'll Own


Experimentation rigor: test design, power and sample-size calls, significance and readout standards. Core of the role: you catch underpowered tests and false positives before they become bad decisions, and you get Growth's tests onto the anytime-valid monitoring the program already runs, so early calls come from a crossed boundary instead of a hopeful trend read
The self-serve experimentation layer: automated Growth metrics in Lightdash, Python-backed stat-sig tooling, and the AI skills (Claude routines) already handling pre-test power calcs and live-test health checks. You extend these and keep the layer correct as product and tracking evolve
The Growth funnel model: a trusted, instrumented view of visitor → lead → customer across every brand and channel, with the CAC, LTV, and conversion-rate cuts Growth needs to prioritize investment
The Growth analytics function model: by end of Year 1, the standards and playbook that scale this function beyond one person, plus a buy-vs-build recommendation for the experimentation stack (an off-the-shelf stats engine, or extending our own skills and Python). You bring the recommendation; the final call isn't yours alone


Problems to Solve

Tests that can't answer the question they were run for Growth wants more experiments, but volume without rigor produces confident, wrong conclusions. Raising the bar without becoming the bottleneck is the job.

Getting off the manual treadmill Real tooling already exists: test-design helpers, dashboards, AI skills. Most tests are still hands-on and bespoke. How do you extend that automation so routine cases genuinely self-serve?

Making the funnel decision-grade The semantic layer defines the funnel, but instrumentation is uneven across brands and channels, and no one owns the single trusted view. You build it, and you keep it trusted.

Turning analysis into decisions The hard part isn't the SQL. It's getting a PM or marketer to change course. Can you deliver insight sharp enough that the room acts, and push back when the data favors the popular but wrong idea?

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)


Rigor is the default. Power calculations are standard practice, early stops on Growth tests come from the anytime-valid boundary rather than a trend read, and the re-run rate (redone for tracking or attribution problems) is down
Routine tests self-serve. Metrics and stat-sig are automated in Lightdash, so the team reads standard results without filing a ticket, and your time goes to the tests that need an analyst
A funnel Growth trusts. The acquisition→conversion funnel is instrumented across every brand and channel; Growth prioritizes off your model, not side spreadsheets
Measurable conversion wins. Your analysis directly drove specific, quantified lifts in the funnel, and you can name them


Who You Are

AI-native. You use AI daily for SQL, dbt, and pressure-testing your analysis, extending the skills already running our experimentation process rather than merely using them. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI or treat your workflow as fixed.

A partner, not a report-writer. You don't wait for a ticket. You sit close to Growth and bring the question before anyone asks it. Skip this one if you want a clear queue with no expectation to push back.

Statistically sharp. Wrong fit if "we hit significance" ends your analysis instead of starting it. Right fit if you have a point of view on test design (power, significance, novelty and interaction effects, when not to test) and can explain a broken experiment in plain terms.

Fluent in experiment instrumentation. You know how Segment events and Flagsmith randomization interact, and catch a tracking problem before a test ships, keeping our re-run rate down. This isn't for you if instrumentation is someone else's job.

Fluent in the funnel. You think in CAC, LTV, and channel economics, and know acquisition data's quirks: attribution messiness, seasonality, channel mix. Skip this one if your background is pure product-feature analytics.

Technically self-sufficient. Wrong fit if you need clean data handed to you. Expert SQL, enough Python to automate the stat-sig math, and comfort in dbt and Lightdash, building your own models without waiting on data engineering.

Influences without authority. PMs and marketers act on what you find because your insight is clear and honest about uncertainty. This isn't for you if you consider the job done once the analysis ships, regardless of outcome.

This Role Is NOT

B2C or music and entertainment industry experience

description:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

Open Role: Graduate Partner Marketing Manager

Marketers at Canonical are brand stewards and demand creators.They transform complex open-source technology into messages, stories and strategies that shape the market understanding of our vision. Some focus on differentiated product and portfolio positioning; others specialize in account-based engagement, partner and alliance messaging, or product-led growth. Whatever their specialization, each marketer works as part of a cross-functional unit, contributing campaigns and insights that help the company learn and grow faster.

We have a bias for action, focus efforts on the most impactful activities and take ownership of our results. We work across long buying cycles, balance storytelling with data, design experiments, track outcomes, and iterate rapidly to find what works.

Marketers at Canonical don’t just promote open source; they amplify it, ensuring our innovations reach the right people, at the right time, with clarity and purpose from developers to decision makers.

Nuestra pasión por construir la nueva era de los medios cobra vida gracias a nuestro compromiso con Ser Extraordinarios, invirtiendo en nuestra gente para inspirar una creatividad transformadora. description:
Marketing Operations & Project Manager | AI & Automation




Company: Speedrack West

Location: Remote — Latin America and Europe

Compensation: $13–$18 USD per hour. $18/hour is the maximum budget for this position.

Commitment: Full-time, 8 hours per day, 40 hours per week

Start date: As soon as possible

Reports to: Marketing Manager

Engagement: Independent contractor

Hubstaff is required: You’ll use Hubstaff to track your working hours, which are reviewed for biweekly hourly payments.

You must be comfortable with time tracking and the company’s monitoring settings, which will be explained before you accept the role.

About Speedrack West

Speedrack West helps businesses solve warehouse storage challenges through pallet rack, custom fabrication, and installation services. Based in North Plains, Oregon, we’ve served customers since 1984 with stocked inventory, in-house fabrication, and our own installation team.

Our marketing team is small, collaborative, and actively building AI into its daily work.

About the role

We’re looking for a hands-on marketer who can turn ideas into delivered campaigns, coordinate a team, and build useful AI workflows.

You’ll work directly with our Marketing Manager, who sets strategy and priorities. You’ll help evaluate ideas, organize execution, resolve blockers, and keep projects moving across design, content, SEO, and paid advertising.

You’ll also build automations and internal tools that reduce repetitive work. Using AI to write content is helpful, but this role requires experience personally building and testing workflows or tools.

What you’ll do

Marketing project and campaign delivery

Turn priorities into project plans, tasks, owners, deadlines, and acceptance criteria.
Coordinate marketing sprints in ClickUp and keep progress visible.
Manage dependencies and workloads, identify blockers, and communicate trade-offs early.
Coordinate contributors across design, content, SEO, and paid advertising.
Review deliverables for accuracy, clear messaging, audience relevance, and quality.
Support hands-on execution when needed while keeping the overall project moving.
Track campaign results and recommend improvements.

AI workflows and automation

Identify recurring tasks that can be automated or simplified.
Build and improve internal tools using Claude Code, Codex, Replit, or similar AI-assisted development tools.
Connect platforms through APIs and automation tools where appropriate.
Develop workflows supporting reporting, content production, campaign execution, and team coordination.
Test outputs, troubleshoot failures, and include appropriate human review.
Document workflows so teammates can use and maintain them.
Collaborate on projects involving conversion optimization, SEO, and paid media analysis.

Website experiments and changes will be coordinated with the Marketing Manager and relevant development support, with scope and approval agreed before implementation.

Team processes and communication

Keep project information, brand guidelines, templates, and procedures organized.
Bring practical ideas and constructive feedback to the Marketing Manager.
Help teammates adopt useful tools and processes.
Own follow-up and communicate when a decision or additional support is needed.

What success looks like in your first 60 days

With onboarding and support from the Marketing Manager, you’ll work toward:

Understanding our campaigns, tools, team responsibilities, and existing processes.
Establishing clear project priorities, owners, deadlines, and reporting.
Taking responsibility for team follow-up and helping resolve blockers.
Building or improving an initial AI workflow with agreed scope and measurable value.

What we’re looking for

3+ years of hands-on marketing experience, including campaigns you helped create and launch.
Experience coordinating projects with multiple contributors.
Strong understanding of audiences, positioning, messaging, customer journeys, and campaign performance.
Experience managing work in ClickUp, Asana, Monday.com, or a similar platform.
Regular use of AI tools in your work.
At least one automation or internal tool you personally built and tested.
Practical experience with AI-assisted coding.
Clear written and spoken English.
Strong ownership, sound judgment, and reliable follow-through.
Ability to work independently while collaborating closely with a manager and team.

You don’t need to be a software engineer. You do need to explain what you built, how it works, how you verified it, and what happens when it fails.

Experience that helps you stand out

B2B, industrial, manufacturing, or home services marketing.
HubSpot or GoHighLevel.
Make, n8n, or Zapier.
APIs, dashboards, and automated reporting.
Internal knowledge hubs or reusable AI workflows.
Basic design skills using Canva, Figma, or similar tools.

Working arrangements

We welcome applicants based in Latin America and Europe who can work 40 hours per week and maintain agreed overlap with our U.S.-based team.

Scheduling is flexible around required meetings and team coordination. We’re hiring an individual who will personally perform the work, rather than an agency service.

We’re looking to fill this role quickly, so please include your earliest available start date.

Marketing, Sales & Communications Experts to contribute to a customer’s project focused on high-impact business presentations. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.




Scope of Work

1. Receive images of business slides related to marketing, sales, and communications materials and reconstruct them in Microsoft PowerPoint.

2. Elevate slides by enhancing visual design, data visualization, and storytelling while preserving factual accuracy and domain-specific definitions.

3. Write a detailed log for each slide, clearly explaining both improvements made and intentional choices to preserve elements, defending strong original decisions as needed.

4. Work with various presentation types, including campaign performance reviews, brand strategies, sales pitch decks, and executive board or investor communications.

5. Apply critical thinking, content editing, and written communication skills to clarify messaging, structure, and evidence-supported points.

6. Ensure that revised slides reflect best practices in marketing, sales enablement, and corporate communications without diluting core industry caveats or context.




Preferred Qualifications

1. 3+ years of hands-on experience in marketing, brand, sales enablement, corporate communications, or relevant agency environments.

2. Demonstrated expertise in building executive-level presentations for senior leaders or client stakeholders.

3. Advanced proficiency with Microsoft PowerPoint, including layout, visual hierarchy, and data visualization best practices.

4. Strong critical thinking and attention to detail; able to articulate the rationale for both improvements and preserved elements.

5. Exceptional written communication skills, with the capacity to explain messaging hierarchy and exhibit choices in a clear, concise manner.

6. Direct industry or practitioner experience valued more than a consulting-firm background; both industry contributors and consultants are welcomed.

7. Prior experience with AI training, evaluation, or rubric development is a plus, though not required.

This Is Not a New-Business Sales Role

description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

 

About the role:

The Engagement Services Consultant (ESC), Integrations is a new, consultant-level role within Samsara's Engagement Services team in Customer Success. You will partner directly with our largest Enterprise customers in a focused, roughly three-month engagement to understand their operational processes, map how those processes connect to the Samsara platform, and translate that understanding into a well-defined, build-ready request for our Solutions Integration Services (SIS) team.

This role complements the Engagement Services Manager (ESM) and SIS teams. It ensures every integration request reaches SIS with validated requirements, aligned stakeholders, and documented processes. This role can be office-based or fully remote.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in Mexico

 

You should apply if:

You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

In this role, you will: 

. Discover and define processes (weeks 1–6)

Run structured discovery with customer stakeholders to document current-state processes and systems.
Facilitate workshops to map future-state process flows and identify where data must be sent, received, or transformed.
Build a systems and API inventory covering data volumes, authentication constraints, and regulatory or data-residency considerations.
Engage SIS early for lightweight feasibility checks so blockers surface before build.
 Package requirements (weeks 6–10)
Turn findings into a prioritized requirements package: use cases, field-level data mappings, success criteria, and open risks.
Validate the package with customer stakeholders and the internal account team (CSM, ESM, Sales Engineer).
Complete and submit the SIS Request Log so scoping starts from a validated baseline.
 Hand off and transition (weeks 10–12)
Join the initial SIS/ESM scoping meeting to preserve context and answer requirements questions directly.
Support the ESM during SOW drafting where scope or customer intent needs clarification.
Formally close the discovery engagement once SIS and the ESM confirm the request is ready for build, with documentation handed off in full.

Ongoing

Track engagement status, milestones, and timelines in Salesforce and Compass.
Maintain a library of discovery templates and playbooks by integration type, and share lessons learned with the teams that originate requests.
Champion Samsara's cultural principles: Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE


Speed - Short time from kickoff to a request SIS accepts without further scoping clarification
Quality - Requests that need no rework during SIS and ESM scoping.
Cycle time - Faster path from Request Log to signed SOW compared with baseline.
Customer experience - Strong discovery-phase CSAT and feedback from Enterprise stakeholders.
Portfolio impact - More Enterprise accounts moving from an unscoped integration need to a signed, in-build SIS project each quarter.

Minimum requirements for the role:

7+ years in a customer-facing consulting, business/systems analysis, solutions consulting, or implementation role, ideally in enterprise SaaS or IoT software.
Experience running structured discovery with enterprise customers: stakeholder interviews, current- vs. future-state process mapping, and requirements gathering.
Working understanding of APIs and system-integration concepts; comfortable in technical conversations without needing to write integration code.
Strong facilitation, synthesis, and documentation skills, with the ability to turn cross-functional conversations into an actionable requirements document.
Track record managing multi-month, multi-stakeholder engagements independently, with ownership of timeline and quality.

An ideal candidate also has:

Experience with integrations involving fleet/telematics, ERP, WMS, TMS/dispatch, HRIS, or fuel-card systems.
Familiarity with Salesforce and services/project-tracking tools.
Background as a Solutions Consultant, Sales/Solutions Engineer, Professional Services consultant, or Business/Systems Analyst.
Experience supporting Mexico and broader LatAm Enterprise accounts.

YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

Shadow the ESM and SIS teams on 2–3 active integration engagements to learn the Request Log, scoping, and SOW process end to end.
Complete SIS Office Hours and Request Log training, and review prior SIS project documentation for common integration patterns.
Take ownership of a first discovery engagement with an Enterprise account, with an ESM as coach.
Deliver a first fully validated requirements package and SIS Request Log independently by the end of the quarter.
 

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

Somos Movizzon una empresa de tecnología especializada en monitoreo sintético de canales digitales. ¿Qué estamos buscando?

Buscamos a alguien con perfil técnico y visión de cliente para ejecutar y liderar la implementación y atención de nuestros servicios de monitoreo en México, alguien que sepa "meter las manos" en lo técnico, pero que también sea capaz de traducir esto a lenguaje de negocio para el cliente.

Actuar como socio estratégico y defensor técnico del cliente en México: implementar, configurar y atender en tiempo real los flujos de monitoreo de sus canales digitales, liderando la resolución de incidentes y movilizando internamente a los equipos necesarios sin depender de aprobaciones adicionales, para asegurar la correcta entrega del servicio comprometido (alertas, dashboards e informes).

Liderar de forma multidisciplinaria (ejecutor y negociador)

description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

 

About the role:

Our Customer Success Managers pick up where our Implementation team leaves off, working closely with our customers to understand their fleet and unique challenges, advising on how to customize Samsara for their needs, and becoming their long-term partner.

Your role will be cross-functional in nature, working alongside and connecting Sales, Support, Sales Engineering and Product, enabling you to experience multiple aspects of a hyper-growth company from within.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in Mexico. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role. This position requires travel up to 30% of the time.

You should apply if:

You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will: 

Be on the front-lines and ensure our customers increase the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of their operations with our IoT platform
Compose joint success plans with customers, outlining their objectives, metrics, timelines, and effectively removing any barriers to achieving business value
Orchestrate renewal-focused business reviews with our customers where we look back at past successes and align on upcoming goals
Deeply understand the Samsara platform’s capabilities and explain them to businesses of all types - field services, utilities, long-haul transportation, school buses, and many more
Mitigate escalations and resolve customer issues
Help Customers with a wide range of general inquiries and questions
Solve customer issues and escalations about Samsara products and services
Experience in multi-channel servicing including excellent phone skills and good writing skills for Web, email, and channel requests
Ability to prioritize work queue and backlog in addition to incoming customer requests
Provide excellent customer service throughout the service cycle from initial request to final close out of the transaction
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

Minimum requirements for the role:

2-5 years of experience in a Customer Success, account management, or consulting role. SaaS experience preferred
Experience supporting or working with technical products
Solutions-oriented with strong problem-solving skills
Passion for going above and beyond the call of duty, taking initiative, and thriving in a fast-paced, change-heavy environment
Bachelor’s degree from a 4-year institution
Spanish and English fluency
IA tools fluency (Claude/ Pilot/ Gemini, others)

An ideal candidate also has:

Has strong bias for standardization & automation, the ability to think big, with insistence on high standards
Thrives in a fast-paced and change-heavy environment
 

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations 

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

description:
About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care into the one-stop shop for all home services. Getting there depends on how fast we can test, learn, and scale what works.

About The Data Team

We're a high-leverage team of Product Data Analysts embedded across the business, owning the semantic layer and the metrics everyone trusts. The experimentation program runs on real rigor, not vibes: pre-registered analysis plans gate every test launch, anytime-valid statistics keep mid-run dashboards honest under continuous viewing, automated daily SRM and attribution health sweeps catch broken tests early, and seasonal power forecasting accounts for a business that swings hard by time of year. The test lifecycle, design through readout, is already AI-driven. Our analysts are stretched across product, so Growth support has stayed part-time and reactive, until now.

The Role

You're the first data analyst dedicated entirely to Growth and Experimentation. Your primary charter is the experimentation program: test design, statistical rigor, and readouts across web funnels, SMS/drip, sales-driven tests, and SEO tests built on our own page-clustering tooling. It's a wider surface than most companies run. You also own the acquisition-to-conversion funnel those tests move, across paid, organic, and partner channels. What to test and which direction to bet on is the CRO's and Growth PMs' call; you shape it, they decide it.

You're not starting from scratch. Dashboards, tooling, and rigor scaffolding are already shipped and running. Expect the early months to be hands-on and manual: scoping tests, crunching readouts, while you build toward a self-serve layer. If a test readout and a funnel refresh ever compete for your week, the test wins.

What Makes This Role Different


The CEO personally engages with test design here: real organizational weight, no fight for buy-in
You partner directly with the Director of CRO, performance marketing, and Growth PMs, who come to you when a test needs a call


Requirements

What You'll Own


Experimentation rigor: test design, power and sample-size calls, significance and readout standards. Core of the role: you catch underpowered tests and false positives before they become bad decisions, and you get Growth's tests onto the anytime-valid monitoring the program already runs, so early calls come from a crossed boundary instead of a hopeful trend read
The self-serve experimentation layer: automated Growth metrics in Lightdash, Python-backed stat-sig tooling, and the AI skills (Claude routines) already handling pre-test power calcs and live-test health checks. You extend these and keep the layer correct as product and tracking evolve
The Growth funnel model: a trusted, instrumented view of visitor → lead → customer across every brand and channel, with the CAC, LTV, and conversion-rate cuts Growth needs to prioritize investment
The Growth analytics function model: by end of Year 1, the standards and playbook that scale this function beyond one person, plus a buy-vs-build recommendation for the experimentation stack (an off-the-shelf stats engine, or extending our own skills and Python). You bring the recommendation; the final call isn't yours alone


Problems to Solve

Tests that can't answer the question they were run for Growth wants more experiments, but volume without rigor produces confident, wrong conclusions. Raising the bar without becoming the bottleneck is the job.

Getting off the manual treadmill Real tooling already exists: test-design helpers, dashboards, AI skills. Most tests are still hands-on and bespoke. How do you extend that automation so routine cases genuinely self-serve?

Making the funnel decision-grade The semantic layer defines the funnel, but instrumentation is uneven across brands and channels, and no one owns the single trusted view. You build it, and you keep it trusted.

Turning analysis into decisions The hard part isn't the SQL. It's getting a PM or marketer to change course. Can you deliver insight sharp enough that the room acts, and push back when the data favors the popular but wrong idea?

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)


Rigor is the default. Power calculations are standard practice, early stops on Growth tests come from the anytime-valid boundary rather than a trend read, and the re-run rate (redone for tracking or attribution problems) is down
Routine tests self-serve. Metrics and stat-sig are automated in Lightdash, so the team reads standard results without filing a ticket, and your time goes to the tests that need an analyst
A funnel Growth trusts. The acquisition→conversion funnel is instrumented across every brand and channel; Growth prioritizes off your model, not side spreadsheets
Measurable conversion wins. Your analysis directly drove specific, quantified lifts in the funnel, and you can name them


Who You Are

AI-native. You use AI daily for SQL, dbt, and pressure-testing your analysis, extending the skills already running our experimentation process rather than merely using them. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI or treat your workflow as fixed.

A partner, not a report-writer. You don't wait for a ticket. You sit close to Growth and bring the question before anyone asks it. Skip this one if you want a clear queue with no expectation to push back.

Statistically sharp. Wrong fit if "we hit significance" ends your analysis instead of starting it. Right fit if you have a point of view on test design (power, significance, novelty and interaction effects, when not to test) and can explain a broken experiment in plain terms.

Fluent in experiment instrumentation. You know how Segment events and Flagsmith randomization interact, and catch a tracking problem before a test ships, keeping our re-run rate down. This isn't for you if instrumentation is someone else's job.

Fluent in the funnel. You think in CAC, LTV, and channel economics, and know acquisition data's quirks: attribution messiness, seasonality, channel mix. Skip this one if your background is pure product-feature analytics.

Technically self-sufficient. Wrong fit if you need clean data handed to you. Expert SQL, enough Python to automate the stat-sig math, and comfort in dbt and Lightdash, building your own models without waiting on data engineering.

Influences without authority. PMs and marketers act on what you find because your insight is clear and honest about uncertainty. This isn't for you if you consider the job done once the analysis ships, regardless of outcome.

This Role Is NOT


A ticket queue. Not the role if you want well-defined asks: no one hands you a backlog of number-pulls, you decide what's worth measuring
The person who decides what to test. You shape that call and own its rigor, but the roadmap and final direction belong to the CRO and Growth PMs
A product-feature analyst seat. Existing analysts already own product, pricing, and service delivery; this one lives in Growth: acquisition, conversion, experimentation
A pure platform or dashboard-builder. You'll automate metrics, stat-sig, and AI skills into a self-serve layer, but that's the means. The job is designing experiments and keeping that automation correct as product and tracking evolve
A people-management role. This is an individual-contributor seat


Benefits


Base salary: $75,000-$100,000 USD annually
The scope is the draw: First analyst dedicated entirely to Growth and Experimentation, with your fingerprints on how this company decides what works
AI tooling provided: The Claude routines already running pieces of our experimentation process are yours to extend, not a side project you have to justify
Fully remote: This is deep-focus analytical work with US-facing partners. We hire the best analyst regardless of city and trust you to manage your environment and overlap hours
Flexible PTO: Measured on outcomes, not hours logged

Identify missing information, inconsistencies, and unsuitable recommendations, applying editorial judgment throughout the process.
Writing and Editorial Quality
Ensure every article addresses the reader's search intent and provides clear, relevant, and useful information.
Rewrite generic or unnatural AI-generated passages into specific, engaging, and human-sounding content.
Maintain a consistent editorial voice using clear language, short sentences, and American English spelling.
Proofread existing articles for grammar, readability, clarity, and factual accuracy.
Fact-Checking and Research
Verify legal, tax, payroll, and other regulatory information using reliable official government sources.
Confirm that all figures and factual statements are current and accurate.
Add relevant inline links to official sources to support important claims.
SEO, GEO, and Content Optimization
Apply SEO and GEO guidelines to keyword placement, headings, FAQ sections, and internal linking.
Ensure article structures are optimized for traditional search engines and AI-powered search tools.
Prepare and optimize visual assets by sourcing images through Canva, converting them to WebP format under 150 KB, and writing descriptive alt text.
Collaboration and Revisions
Submit completed articles to the content lead for review.
Incorporate feedback and complete up to two rounds of revisions per article.
Meet agreed delivery deadlines and maintain consistent quality across assignments.
Native-level English writing and editing skills, with excellent grammar and a natural, polished writing style.
Strong working knowledge of SEO principles, including search intent, keyword placement, and heading structure.
Understanding of GEO and how AI-powered search tools discover, interpret, and present content.
Hands-on experience using AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT for professional content creation.
Ability to identify generic, inaccurate, or unnatural AI-generated text and rewrite it into clear, human-sounding content.
Strong fact-checking and research skills, including the ability to locate and interpret official government sources.
Excellent attention to detail and the ability to assess the accuracy, relevance, and completeness of content.
Ability to manage assignments independently and meet deadlines.
Previous B2B content writing experience, particularly in HR technology, fintech, or SaaS.
Familiarity with Google's E-E-A-T principles: Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness.
Basic knowledge of global remote work, international employment, cross-border compliance, payroll, or Employer of Record (EOR) services.
Experience with prompt-based or multi-step AI content workflows.
Familiarity with SEO tools such as Ahrefs, SEMrush, or Ubersuggest.
Access to a Canva Pro account for sourcing a wider range of visual assets.

Full article, from brief to final draft including images: starting at USD 50.

Flexible, project-based collaboration.

You will work with topics related to international employment, payroll, compliance, and global workforce management. Role Title: Research Marketing Lead (Remote)

The Role

We’re looking for a Research Marketing Lead to own how our research, benchmarks, and technical work are positioned, launched, and adopted across the AI ecosystem.




You’ll work closely with our research team to turn technical work into high-impact launches that earn attention, adoption, and citations. You’ll develop a deep understanding of our research and methodology, shape positioning and narratives, establish a high quality bar for publication, and build go-to-market strategies that put our work in front of the right researchers, developers, AI labs, and technical audiences.




What You'll Do

1. Own research GTM end-to-end, developing launch and distribution strategies for research, benchmarks, evaluations, and other technical work.

2. Establish the publication-readiness bar for research and benchmarks, partnering with researchers to ensure methodology, claims, results, and supporting materials are rigorous, clear, and defensible before launch.

3. Develop positioning and narratives that translate complex technical findings into clear, differentiated stories without sacrificing technical accuracy or depth.

4. Identify high-impact research opportunities by understanding emerging AI trends, open questions, competitive research, and what matters to researchers and practitioners.

5. Shape research packaging and distribution, including research pages, benchmark releases, technical content, launch materials, and other assets that drive discovery and usage.

6. Build relationships across the AI research ecosystem, including researchers, AI labs, developers, technical communities, and influential practitioners.

7. Drive adoption of our research and benchmarks, identifying the audiences, communities, and channels most likely to use, reference, and build on our work.

8. Measure research impact, tracking adoption, citations, engagement, usage, and qualitative feedback to understand what resonates and where our work is creating value.

9. Create feedback loops between the market and research, bringing ecosystem insights back to the research team to inform future benchmarks, evaluations, and research priorities.




What We're Looking For

1. Experience marketing, launching, or driving adoption of technical research, AI/ML products, developer products, benchmarks, evaluations, or similarly complex technical work.

2. Strong track record developing and executing go-to-market strategies for technical audiences.

3. Ability to deeply understand technical work and translate it into clear, credible, differentiated positioning and narratives.

4. Strong understanding of the AI/ML research ecosystem, including major labs, research trends, benchmarks, evaluations, and technical communities.

5. Exceptional written communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with both highly technical and broader audiences.

6. Strong analytical judgment and the ability to evaluate whether technical claims, supporting evidence, and research materials are ready for external publication.

7. Experience building relationships with researchers, technical leaders, developers, or AI communities.

8. High ownership and the ability to take ambiguous initiatives from strategy through execution.

About Crunchyroll

Founded by fans, Crunchyroll delivers the art and culture of anime to a passionate community. We super-serve over 100 million anime and manga fans across 200+ countries and territories, and help them connect with the stories and characters they crave. Whether that experience is online or in-person, streaming video, theatrical, games, merchandise, events and more, it’s powered by the anime content we all love.

Crunchyroll, LLC is an independently operated joint venture between US-based Sony Pictures Entertainment, and Japan's Aniplex, a subsidiary of Sony Music Entertainment (Japan) Inc., both subsidiaries of Tokyo-based Sony Group Corporation.

About The Role

The General Manager, Latin America (LATAM) is accountable for the long-term health, growth, and operating performance of Crunchyroll's business across the region. As Crunchyroll's senior business leader in LATAM reporting into Crunchyroll’s Chief Operating Officer, the GM brings together commercial leadership, regional operations, growth, partnerships, communications, localization, and fan engagement – at the regional level – into a single operating model focused on delivering sustainable business performance.

LATAM is a market of meaningful scale for Crunchyroll, with an established business and infrastructure as well as significant opportunity for continued growth. The GM will be responsible for accelerating growth by optimizing existing levers while identifying, testing, and scaling new opportunities across the region.

The GM will also ensure that local insights from teams closest to the market inform broader business decisions, creating a clear path for regional consumer trends, market dynamics, and commercial opportunities to shape Crunchyroll’s strategy and priorities.

Este/a líder es el/la experto/a más senior de Fictiv en materia de fundición: alguien que ha diseñado, lanzado o liderado personalmente programas de fundición desde el diseño hasta la producción, y actúa como el vínculo estratégico y técnico dentro de la empresa, definiendo cómo cotizamos, cómo comercializamos, cómo ganamos en los mercados y qué capacidades desarrollamos dentro de nuestra red de socios de manufactura. El/la Director/a aplica una profunda experiencia práctica en fundición para tomar decisiones informadas sobre precios, posicionamiento, inversión en capacidades y estrategia de socios, así como para interactuar de manera creíble con cualquier socio, cliente o equipo técnico en los problemas de fundición más complejos. Este rol es responsable de la visión, estrategia y crecimiento rentable de ingresos en una cartera técnicamente diversa e intensiva en herramentales. El éxito requiere operar con una mentalidad proactiva de construcción de negocio: anticipar riesgos y oportunidades, hacer recomendaciones audaces y traducir conocimientos del mercado, técnicos y del cliente en acciones decisivas en ventas, marketing, ingeniería de soluciones, gestión de programas y gerentes generales regionales.

Áreas de Responsabilidad:

Operar como el/la dueño/a emprendedor/a de la línea de negocio de fundición en fundición a presión, fundición de inversión y fundición en arena, con responsabilidad sobre la visión, estrategia, crecimiento y resultados.

Sintetizar proactivamente tendencias de mercado, necesidades de clientes, inteligencia competitiva e información interna para informar la estrategia, identificar oportunidades y riesgos, e impulsar acciones decisivas.

Definir y evolucionar la estrategia de línea de producto, precios y posicionamiento go-to-market en fundición a presión, fundición de inversión y fundición en arena para entregar crecimiento rentable de ingresos, sólido desempeño de margen y mayor valor para el cliente.

Dar forma al roadmap de capacidades de fundición de Fictiv: definiendo qué procesos, aleaciones, clases de tolerancia, tamaños de pieza, certificaciones y operaciones secundarias soportar; identificando brechas de capacidad en la red de socios de manufactura; y estableciendo estándares de calificación e incorporación, en colaboración con Ingeniería de Soluciones, Programa y Gerentes Generales regionales.

Influir y alinear a socios multifuncionales en ventas, marketing, ingeniería de soluciones, gestión de programas y éxito del cliente para ejecutar la estrategia y entregar resultados.

Actuar como el/la experto/a interno/a de Fictiv en fundición, cubriendo Diseño para Fundición (DFC), selección de aleaciones y procesos, consideraciones de herramentales, principios de alimentación y solidificación, modos de defectos, realidades de tolerancias y operaciones secundarias; habilitando precisión en cotizaciones, interacción con ventas, conversaciones técnicas con clientes y revisión informada de aportaciones y capacidades de socios de manufactura.

Establecer y dar seguimiento a métricas clave de crecimiento, margen, conversión de cotización a orden, entrega a tiempo, aprobación de primer artículo y satisfacción del cliente; comunicar avances e insights de manera efectiva a stakeholders técnicos y no técnicos.

Fomentar la rendición de cuentas mediante la mejora continua, el cuestionamiento de supuestos y el aseguramiento de la alineación con los objetivos del negocio.

Experiencia Preferida / Calificaciones Mínimas:

Licenciatura en Ingeniería Mecánica, de Materiales, Metalúrgica o de Manufactura, Administración de Operaciones o campo relacionado; se prefiere maestría.

Más de 10 años de experiencia práctica en fundición de metales, abarcando fundición a presión, fundición de inversión y/o fundición en arena, con responsabilidad directa en fundición, ingeniería o procesos, y más de 5 años en un rol de liderazgo responsable de crecimiento, operaciones o desarrollo de negocio.

Experiencia profunda en procesos y tecnologías de fundición, incluyendo fundición a presión de alta presión (HPDC), fundición a presión de baja presión, fundición de inversión o cera perdida y fundición en arena; sólido dominio de selección de aleaciones —aluminio, zinc, magnesio, aceros inoxidables y al carbono, aleaciones ferrosas—, alimentación y solidificación, diseño y vida de herramentales y moldes/patrones, mecanismos y controles de defectos —porosidad, contracción, juntas frías, inclusiones, llenado incompleto— y operaciones secundarias —tratamiento térmico, maquinado, NDT, acabado superficial—. Familiaridad con ISO 9001, IATF 16949, AS9100, NADCA, ASTM y estándares ambientales.

Capacidad demostrada para impulsar crecimiento de negocio, estrategia comercial y satisfacción del cliente en un entorno multiproceso e intensivo en herramentales; es esencial sentirse cómodo/a operando a través de una red distribuida de socios de manufactura.

Excelentes habilidades de liderazgo, comunicación y colaboración, con la capacidad de alinear e inspirar a stakeholders diversos.

description:
About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care into the one-stop shop for all home services. Getting there depends on how fast we can test, learn, and scale what works.

About The Data Team

We're a high-leverage team of Product Data Analysts embedded across the business, owning the semantic layer and the metrics everyone trusts. The experimentation program runs on real rigor, not vibes: pre-registered analysis plans gate every test launch, anytime-valid statistics keep mid-run dashboards honest under continuous viewing, automated daily SRM and attribution health sweeps catch broken tests early, and seasonal power forecasting accounts for a business that swings hard by time of year. The test lifecycle, design through readout, is already AI-driven. Our analysts are stretched across product, so Growth support has stayed part-time and reactive, until now.

The Role

You're the first data analyst dedicated entirely to Growth and Experimentation. Your primary charter is the experimentation program: test design, statistical rigor, and readouts across web funnels, SMS/drip, sales-driven tests, and SEO tests built on our own page-clustering tooling. It's a wider surface than most companies run. You also own the acquisition-to-conversion funnel those tests move, across paid, organic, and partner channels. What to test and which direction to bet on is the CRO's and Growth PMs' call; you shape it, they decide it.

You're not starting from scratch. Dashboards, tooling, and rigor scaffolding are already shipped and running. Expect the early months to be hands-on and manual: scoping tests, crunching readouts, while you build toward a self-serve layer. If a test readout and a funnel refresh ever compete for your week, the test wins.

What Makes This Role Different


The CEO personally engages with test design here: real organizational weight, no fight for buy-in
You partner directly with the Director of CRO, performance marketing, and Growth PMs, who come to you when a test needs a call


Requirements

What You'll Own


Experimentation rigor: test design, power and sample-size calls, significance and readout standards. Core of the role: you catch underpowered tests and false positives before they become bad decisions, and you get Growth's tests onto the anytime-valid monitoring the program already runs, so early calls come from a crossed boundary instead of a hopeful trend read
The self-serve experimentation layer: automated Growth metrics in Lightdash, Python-backed stat-sig tooling, and the AI skills (Claude routines) already handling pre-test power calcs and live-test health checks. You extend these and keep the layer correct as product and tracking evolve
The Growth funnel model: a trusted, instrumented view of visitor → lead → customer across every brand and channel, with the CAC, LTV, and conversion-rate cuts Growth needs to prioritize investment
The Growth analytics function model: by end of Year 1, the standards and playbook that scale this function beyond one person, plus a buy-vs-build recommendation for the experimentation stack (an off-the-shelf stats engine, or extending our own skills and Python). You bring the recommendation; the final call isn't yours alone


Problems to Solve

Tests that can't answer the question they were run for Growth wants more experiments, but volume without rigor produces confident, wrong conclusions. Raising the bar without becoming the bottleneck is the job.

Getting off the manual treadmill Real tooling already exists: test-design helpers, dashboards, AI skills. Most tests are still hands-on and bespoke. How do you extend that automation so routine cases genuinely self-serve?

Making the funnel decision-grade The semantic layer defines the funnel, but instrumentation is uneven across brands and channels, and no one owns the single trusted view. You build it, and you keep it trusted.

Turning analysis into decisions The hard part isn't the SQL. It's getting a PM or marketer to change course. Can you deliver insight sharp enough that the room acts, and push back when the data favors the popular but wrong idea?

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)


Rigor is the default. Power calculations are standard practice, early stops on Growth tests come from the anytime-valid boundary rather than a trend read, and the re-run rate (redone for tracking or attribution problems) is down
Routine tests self-serve. Metrics and stat-sig are automated in Lightdash, so the team reads standard results without filing a ticket, and your time goes to the tests that need an analyst
A funnel Growth trusts. The acquisition→conversion funnel is instrumented across every brand and channel; Growth prioritizes off your model, not side spreadsheets
Measurable conversion wins. Your analysis directly drove specific, quantified lifts in the funnel, and you can name them


Who You Are

AI-native. You use AI daily for SQL, dbt, and pressure-testing your analysis, extending the skills already running our experimentation process rather than merely using them. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI or treat your workflow as fixed.

A partner, not a report-writer. You don't wait for a ticket. You sit close to Growth and bring the question before anyone asks it. Skip this one if you want a clear queue with no expectation to push back.

Statistically sharp. Wrong fit if "we hit significance" ends your analysis instead of starting it. Right fit if you have a point of view on test design (power, significance, novelty and interaction effects, when not to test) and can explain a broken experiment in plain terms.

Fluent in experiment instrumentation. You know how Segment events and Flagsmith randomization interact, and catch a tracking problem before a test ships, keeping our re-run rate down. This isn't for you if instrumentation is someone else's job.

Fluent in the funnel. You think in CAC, LTV, and channel economics, and know acquisition data's quirks: attribution messiness, seasonality, channel mix. Skip this one if your background is pure product-feature analytics.

Technically self-sufficient. Wrong fit if you need clean data handed to you. Expert SQL, enough Python to automate the stat-sig math, and comfort in dbt and Lightdash, building your own models without waiting on data engineering.

Influences without authority. PMs and marketers act on what you find because your insight is clear and honest about uncertainty. This isn't for you if you consider the job done once the analysis ships, regardless of outcome.
